prompts.day-prompt.txt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: UPDATED PHONE wallpaper concept for the existing Sunken Teahouse project. One full portrait illustration, intended aspect 6:13, requested 1440x3120. No phone bezel, UI, text, labels or collage.
Input image 1: the earlier PHONE composition, reference for the recognizable blue-yellow drawn scout fish, modest red/beige crab, lavender drawn octopus, small hermit and submerged Japanese timber identity. Input image 2: the finished DESKTOP reference for PHOTO QUALITY weathered wood, real architectural perspective, physical materials, combined with deliberately hand-drawn cel-shaded inhabitants. The new portrait must have its own architecture and composition.
PRIMARY REQUEST: A SUBMERGED TEAHOUSE-PAGODA, seen at intimate three-quarter angle with open stacked terraces. A narrow old timber pagoda pavilion rising through blue-green water, with two visible open inhabited/display levels and three graceful overlapping eaves. It is a real coherent photographic building with open sides, viewed close enough to read its lower household scene on a SMALL PHONE SCREEN. The whole building is underwater, inside and outside. One continuous camera, one common light; upper ledges and eaves above eye level show undersides, lower tea floor below eye level shows its top. No dollhouse cutaway and no separate stacked panels.
PHONE COMPOSITION:
Upper 0–23%: calm open blue-green water and restrained sunshafts, quiet center for a clock; very sparse distant shoal only near upper right. The highest pagoda eave starts around 24–27%, not behind the top clock. No close face or essential reward in the top fifth.
Middle 28–61%: the pagoda's upper gallery and weather architecture. Dark indigo weathered photographic columns and beams, gently curved eaves, restrained old brass. The wall infill on its upper level is a BROAD visible warm amber/ivory decorative panel with a large simple opened-fan / sun-and-ripple motif, spanning enough area to read as a major shape at 360px width. This panel is the weather/temperature signal, not a tiny ornament. Do not uniformly recolor the timber or characters. Below and staggered across the gallery: only TWO large physical weather objects, a round sealed stoppered clear cyan glass vessel with a conspicuous LOW colored-liquid level on a real narrow ledge, and a photographic open ivory-pink clam with one pearl on a lower left ledge. Add one simple hanging shell/ribbon mobile near a side column for current direction. Avoid rows of miniature porcelain, tiny gauges, duplicate fan objects and the old giant left-hand cabinet. The small moon mirror may be mounted on an edge beam outside the central clock region.
Lower 61–88%: the open LOWER TEA TERRACE with inhabitants, immediately readable at 360px wide. Same modest drawn red crab center-left, BODY width only 22–25% of the frame, face near 74%, feet near 80%; two clear eyes, relaxed low claws. Same friendly round blue/yellow drawn scout fish above the floor in the open water at center-right around 65%, width about 23%; same lavender drawn octopus on a real low wooden right tea table, face near 75%, width about 22%. A blue-and-white porcelain cup is firmly held by its tentacle; 2 or 3 grouped cups sit directly on the tabletop, no gap. One small secondary hermit in a lotus jar can sit at the far left of this terrace, clearly separate from crab and table. Keep the FLOOR shallow enough that inhabitants sit in the lower portion, not an unnecessarily empty lower third. Leave a completely open water passage between gallery and lower terrace at center, which can later accommodate one rare night guest. Do not put a foreground handrail across faces; the rear railing must sit clearly behind the opaque inhabitants.
Bottom 10–12%: lower structural base/steps fading into water and a quiet foreground, no face or essential action flush against the bottom. Side margins tolerate modest cropping. Heroes may occupy the lower terrace; their faces and rewards are kept above the extreme bottom strip.
MIXED REALITY: Photo-quality realistic submerged wood, panels, fabric, glass, ceramic and metal. Main inhabitants remain drawn 2D characters, consistent with desktop; the photographic architecture must NOT turn into an oil painting or cartoon. Fixed coherent vanishing directions: frames align to walls and beams, cups and clam meet supports with contact shading and front-lip occlusion. No floating vessel or bowl, no unsupported shelf. Avoid hot dry terrestrial spotlights and a glossy wet floor.
UNDERWATER CUES: fine suspended particles distributed through the room and exterior, a handful of photographic bubbles at depth and a few clean drawn bubbles close to drawn creatures, broad soft irregular underwater caustics on wood, cyan distance and lower far contrast. No bubbles on eyes, no dense glitter, no thick fog. The wall weather motif is decorative ink/fabric; no real rain or snow falling inside water. Solid bodies remain opaque. Daylight: clear cyan water and controlled warmer bounce, warm upper wall infill gives a readable temperature cue. No humans, mermaids, Gremlin figure, dragon or other large guest in THIS neutral daytime view. All major forms should read at 360px width.
prompts.night-correction-prompt.txt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit this exact NIGHT portrait pagoda. Change ONLY the dragon's scale, pose and placement within the open lower room, plus a restrained deepening of the distant nighttime ambience. Keep all photographic architecture, every beam/column/eave/rail, upper weather panels, weather objects, lower table and cups, the crab/octopus/hermit, and the already relocated left scout fish at exactly the same positions and sizes. Preserve the camera and full portrait crop.
The current dragon is too large and its long whiskers approach the rear rail. Make this SAME jade/cyan, cream-faced, golden-antlered, amber-eyed, pale lilac-maned dragon visibly SMALLER: approximately 65% of its current displayed size. Preserve its identity and face. Keep one single continuous swimming body with the far tail in the right-side exterior water, but the small near head inside the lower open room.
CRITICAL CORRIDOR on this approximately 853x1844 image: place the near HEAD + MANE + WHISKERS entirely inside the open-water rectangle x=355..610, y=1060..1220. The friendly eye is around x=465,y=1140. Keep the lower edge of every near whisker above y=1230, with at least a clearly visible gap to the rear railing, whose top is around y=1250..1310. Shorten and curl the whiskers upward so they stay close to the head, not stretched downward to the rail or crab. Keep the scout fish's entire silhouette untouched and separated at the left; keep octopus, crab, their faces, shells and every cup clear.
The near dragon must NEVER visibly overlap the horizontal rear rail in this concept: it swims ABOVE that rail, below the overhanging upper beam. Its remaining neck curls to the right around the free outer side of the right column, with a restrained tail in the exterior blue water; natural occlusion by the column separates near and far. No body passing through timber, no arbitrary notch, no wood showing through skin. Solid body/mane opaque, distant tail blue-tinted. Do not add a ground shadow, second head, extra tail, wings or another guest.
Make the exterior ambient blue and lower empty foreground about one third dimmer to read as nighttime; retain local soft warm reflections near panels and readable main character faces and the small dragon. This is an atmospheric phone wallpaper, not a close dragon portrait. No other rearrangement, new objects, text, clock, phone or UI.
prompts.night-dragon-prompt.txt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: RARE NIGHT GUEST study for the SAME portrait Sunken Teahouse-Pagoda phone concept.
Image 1 is the edit target: exact finished portrait pagoda scene. Preserve the full composition, photographic building, eaves, columns, wall panel boundaries, supports, ledges, clam, stoppered jar, table, floor, rear railings, the crab/octopus/hermit positions and character identities. This is the same building at night.
Image 2 is the DRAGON IDENTITY reference, the guest character: preserve its long elegant jade/cyan scaled body, cream throat and face, warm amber eye, gold antler-like horns, flowing pale blue/lilac mane and fins, delicate whiskers and friendly knowing expression. It is a drawn magical water dragon, not a western winged beast. Create a SINGLE continuous body in a compact soft vertical S suited to the open lower tea terrace. No duplicated head, detached tail, extra limbs, wings, hats or giant portrait.
NIGHT: quiet deep blue water, soft cool lunar light and a little warm reflected light from the upper decorative panel. Photograph-like wood and materials still legible. Keep all faces locally readable and opaque; no overall near-black image. The large upper wall stays a pale muted silver-blue cloud/wave decorative panel, its same exact plane and frame. No actual moon disk in the quiet central top clock region. Fine suspended particles, a few soft photographic bubbles, several small drawn bubbles near drawn inhabitants, no bubble crossing any eye. Underwater caustics soft and sparse, no dry mirror floor, no terrestrial rain.
SPATIAL STAGING OF THIS ONE RARE GUEST:
- Keep the upper gallery and its weather props untouched. The dragon visits the LOWER OPEN TEA TERRACE from the blue water at the right.
- Its tail and far end remain outside the pavilion in the water to the RIGHT of the right-hand opening column, about x86–96%, y53–63%. Blue distance tint reduces their contrast, but the solid skin is opaque, not a ghost through which wood is visible.
- Its continuous neck comes AROUND THE FREE OUTER SIDE of that right-hand column and INTO the open lower room BELOW the overhanging beam. The NEAR neck cleanly occludes architecture where it passes in front; do not route a solid body straight through any column, beam or handrail. There is no arbitrary horizontal notch or square cutoff in the body.
- The head and pale mane are visibly INSIDE the open lower tea room, near x56–61%, y63–66% of the full frame, head/mane width about 23–26% of the frame. The near body is in front of the rear railings and behind the primary residents. Leave a clear air/water gap from every inhabitant, the floor, table, cups, jar and any hanging ribbon. Whiskers float within the same free corridor; none touches a crab claw, face, shell or cup.
- For THIS visit only, move the SAME blue/yellow scout fish to the left side of the lower opening, about x27–32%, y62–64%, width about 20–21% of frame. It yields the center of the room to the visitor and faces the dragon with a friendly expression. It remains above the hermit, separate from the left column and the crab's eyes. No bag or long cord on the scout in this study.
- The red crab remains around x44%, y75%, octopus remains at the right tea table around x80%, y72%, hermit stays at left. No overlap with their faces or raised-action envelopes. The dragon has no cast ground-contact shadow because it is freely swimming. No beam showing through its face, mane or neck. No turtle or other large guest at the same time.
The overall result should be a warm quiet nighttime visit by the recognizable guest character inside a photographed submerged pagoda with drawn residents. This is a complete portrait scene, no phone, UI, labels, text or montage. Avoid filling the whole phone with the dragon. Maintain a readable small-screen composition and exact continuity with the daytime pagoda.
prompts.night-registration-prompt.txt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Make ONLY a small registration correction to this exact portrait night pagoda concept. Translate the ENTIRE SAME DRAGON UPWARD by about 25 source pixels on this 853x1844 artwork (about 1.4% of the full height). Keep its exact size, identity, pose and continuous body; shift head, mane, whiskers, belly and tail together. The intention is a clearly visible water gap of at least 20 source pixels between the dragon belly/tail and the TOP of the octopus's head, and between every dragon pixel and the horizontal rear railing. Keep the horns below the overhanging beam with clear space. Preserve appropriate occlusion by the stationary RIGHT COLUMN: the far body/tail behind that column is outside in water, the near head remains inside the free lower opening. Do not change any beam, column, railing, floor, panel, jar, clam, table, cup, bubble arrangement, light, camera or crop; do not move, scale or change the crab, left scout fish, octopus or hermit. Do not invent another head or tail or a horizontal rectangular cut in the body. Solid body opaque. This is the same complete portrait night scene, one small upward relocation of the dragon only, no text or UI.
prompts.overcast-prompt.txt:
Use case: lighting-weather.
Asset type: SECOND CONDITION of the SAME PHONE SUNKEN TEAHOUSE-PAGODA concept.
Input image 1 is the exact daytime pagoda composition to edit. Preserve its full portrait frame, camera, beams and eaves, all column positions, gallery geometry, mirror, jar and clam geometry, rear rails, lower floor, every inhabitant's identity, scale, pose, expression and exact location. Especially keep crab, scout, octopus, hermit and all cups in their exact places. This is a readability comparison of weather states, not a different scene.
Change only the visible weather-bearing surfaces and underwater illumination:
1. The LARGE WARM UPPER WALL INFILL panel with a sun over wave arcs becomes a CLEARLY COOL INDIGO-TEAL panel carrying a bold large silver-blue rolling-cloud / flowing-wave motif. Keep its complete original panel boundary and perspective, wooden columns, frieze, decorative edge and frame unchanged. This is ink/paint or woven fabric on a real wall panel; no words, digits or literal icon interface. Main broad temperature/weather state must be obvious at 360px width. Do not recolor the timber into bright blue paint or flatten its material.
2. The same stoppered clear cyan round vessel on its fixed middle gallery ledge now contains a HIGH colored-liquid level (about three quarters), with the one broad float bead visibly higher. Keep every base-contact, neck, lid and support identical. No new vessel and no exterior glow.
3. Replace the subtle mobile's gentle vertical drape by a single coherent sideways tilt toward the left, with the shell cords and ribbon responding together to the stronger water current. Anchoring point is fixed. Stay clear of columns and ledges; do not add extra ribbons.
4. Underwater DAYLIGHT is more diffuse and overcast: reduce direct shafts and caustic contrast, retain soft blue-cyan volume, fine particles and a few bubbles. Keep all main faces readable, solid and opaque. The atmosphere is underwater throughout. The wall motif conveys rainy/cloudy surface weather; no rain streaks or snow falling inside the submerged scene. Keep the pearl clam in its same open state so this pair isolates wall/color/fill/current changes.
Do not change architectural perspective, crop, photographic materials, character designs, their gestures or mouth/eye shapes. No dragon, turtle, whale, dolphin, extra characters, text, clock, icons or labels. One complete portrait art image in the same proportions as the input.
